tools.name: create_signing_envelope
tools.description: Create a FreeSign envelope from a PDF SHA-256 hash. Do not send PDF bytes. The created envelope is NOT yet session-bound — the browser that opens the returned signing_url generates an ECDSA P-256 keypair locally and POSTs the public JWK to /api/envelopes/{id}/session-bind before any protected reques

tools.name: verify_document_hash
tools.description: Find FreeSign receipts matching a local document SHA-256 hash.

tools.name: get_receipt
tools.description: Return the envelope record (including final_pdf_sha256, final_signature_base64url, final_payload_json), per-signer signing receipts, and OpenTimestamps anchor metadata. Evidence only, never PDF bytes.

tools.name: get_ots_proof
tools.description: Return the .ots proof (base64) for a given OpenTimestamps anchor on an envelope. Use the official `ots-cli` to verify offline against Bitcoin block headers. Each seal has two anchors: `kind: "byterange"` commits to the signed document, `kind: "signed_attrs"` commits to SHA-256 of the CMS SignedAttri

tools.name: verify_audit_chain
tools.description: Return an envelope's append-only audit-event hash chain together with a server-computed integrity verdict: every event_hash is recomputed from its canonical material, and the prev_event_hash linkage and per-envelope seq contiguity are checked. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_ots_proof · Private data: verify_document_hash, get_receipt, get_ots_proof · Public sink: create_signing_envelope, get_ots_proof.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_ots_proof · Private data: verify_document_hash, get_receipt, get_ots_proof · Public sink: create_signing_envelope, get_ots_proof

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_ots_proof" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
